<r>Ant.</r> Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

b.5bb5407055:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.

b.bbeef18477:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>S</c>anctórum méritis ínclyta gáudia
Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
Nam gliscit ánimus prómere cántibus
Victórum genus óptimum.

<h>H</h>i sunt quos rétinens mundus inhórruit:
Ipsum nam stérili flore peráridum
Sprevére pénitus, teque secúti sunt,
Rex Christe bone cǽlitus.

<h>H</h>i pro te fúrias atque ferócia
Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
Cessit his lácerans fórtiter úngula,
Nec carpsit penetrália.

<h>C</h>ædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
Non murmur résonat, non querimónia:
Sed corde tácito mens bene cónscia
Consérvat patiéntiam.

<h>Q</h>uæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
Quæ tu Martyribus múnera prǽparas?
Rubri nam flúido sánguine láureis
Ditántur bene fúlgidis.

<h>T</h>e summa Déitas únaque póscimus,
Ut culpas ábluas, nóxia súbtrahas,
Des pacem fámulis, nos quoque glóriam
Per cuncta tibi sǽcula.
Amen.
b.8f273feed7:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!

<h>T</h>hey, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.

<h>L</h>ord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.

<h>W</h>hile they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.

<h>W</h>hat joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!

<h>Y</h>et we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.

Quorum ex sanguine mártires non pauci sæculo sequénti splendide effloruerunt, quos inter recenséntur ex ordine Prædicatórum Hierónymus Hermosilla et Valentínus Bérrio-Ochóa, epíscopi; qui una cum Petro Almédo et Josépho Kang, catechista indígena, anno millésimo octingentésimo sexagesimo primo, stolas suas in sanguine Agni lavérunt.

<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.

<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * majestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ majestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Judex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.

<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

<c>S</c>éptimo Idus Novémbris Luna octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>P</h>atávii deposítio sancti Prosdócimi, qui fuit primus ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopus. Hic, a beáto Petro Apóstolo Epíscopus ordinátus, ad prædicándum Dei verbum ad prædíctam civitátem missus est; ibíque, multis virtútibus et prodígiis corúscans, beáto fine quiévit.
<h>P</h>erúsiæ sancti Herculáni, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
<h>A</h>pud Swelménsem civitátem, in Germánia, pássio sancti Engelbérti, Epíscopi Coloniénsis, qui, cum illuc ex óppido Sosátio ad templum dedicándum pérgeret, a sicáriis intercéptus in via multísque vulnéribus cæsus, gloriósum pro defensióne ecclesiásticæ libertátis et Románæ Ecclésiæ obediéntia martýrium súbiit.
<h>E</h>ódem die sancti Amaránthi Mártyris, qui apud Albigénsem urbem, in Gállia, exácto agónis fidélis cursu, sepúltus, vivit in glória.
<h>M</h>elitínæ, in Arménia, pássio sanctórum Hierónis, Nicándri, Hesýchii et aliórum trigínta; qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Lýsia Prǽside, coronáti sunt.
<h>A</h>mphípoli, in Macedónia, sanctórum Mártyrum Aucti, Tauriónis et Thessalonícæ.
<h>A</h>ncýræ, in Galátia, pássio sanctórum Melasíppi, Antónii et Carínæ, sub Iuliáno Apóstata.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ beáti Achíllæ Epíscopi, qui eruditióne, fide, conversatióne ac móribus fuit insígnis.
<h>I</h>n Frísia deposítio sancti Willibrórdi, Epíscopi Traiecténsis; qui, a beáto Sérgio Papa ordinátus Epíscopus, in Frísia et Dánia Evangélium prædicávit.
<h>M</h>etis, in Gállia, sancti Rufi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>rgentoráti sancti Floréntii Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.311c8d4bdd:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 7th 2027, the 8th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Padua, holy Prosdocimus, the first Bishop of that see, who was ordained Bishop by the blessed Apostle Peter, and sent to preach the Word of God in that city, where he shone with many graces and wonders, and died a blessed death.
<h>A</h>t Perugia, (in the year 547,) the holy martyr Herculanus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Cologne, (in the year 1225,) holy Engelbert, Bishop (of that see), who was contented to suffer martyrdom in defence of the freedom of the Church and of the obedience due to the Church of Rome.
<h>O</h>n the same day the holy martyr Amaranth, who was buried in the city of Albi when the course of his faithful contending was over, but he is alive for evermore in glory.
<h>A</h>t Melitina, in Armenia, the holy martyrs Hiero, Nicander, Hesychius, and thirty others, who were crowned under the President Lysias, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Amphipolis, in Macedonia, the holy martyrs Auctus, Taurion, and Thessalonica.
<h>A</h>t Ancyra, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, the holy martyrs Melasippus, Anthony, and Carina.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, (about the year 313,) blessed Achillas, Bishop (of that see,) eminent for his learning, faith, conversation, and life.
<h>I</h>n Friesland, (in the year 738,) holy Willebrord, (first) Bishop of Utrecht, who was ordained Bishop by blessed Pope Sergius, and preached the Gospel in Friesland and Denmark, whose feast we keep upon the 29th day of this present month.
<h>A</h>t Metz, (about the year 400,) the holy Confessor Rufus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Strasbourg, (about the year 693,) holy Florence, Bishop (of that see, and Founder and Abbot of Haslach and of St. Thomas.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>F</c>amíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut, quæ in sola spe grátiæ cœléstis innítitur, tua semper protectióne muniátur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.00277e10af:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee to keep thy family continually in godliness, that they who do lean only upon the hope of thine heavenly grace, may evermore be defended by thy mighty power.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
